source_evidence.role: identity, authoritative building footprint, floor metadata
source_evidence.provider: Purdue University GIS, BuildingShapesZip4 FeatureServer layer 0
source_evidence.source_date: Not exposed in the feature response
source_evidence.measurement_method: Used the service polygon's single 34-vertex exterior ring. Transformed EPSG:3857 to longitude/latitude, then into the repository's approximate campus frame using the prescribed local conversion. Floor/roof metadata was transcribed; the service does not document units for these attributes.
source_evidence.uncertainty: GIS confirms identity and plan boundary. It is not a survey of façade or roof geometry. The meaning/units of R, Extrution, and the floor elevation fields are undocumented. The asset interprets R=82.2 as feet (25.05 m) because the level sequence is in 12-unit increments; vertical size is an estimate, not a measured height.

source_evidence.role: historic facade form and entrance character
source_evidence.provider: Purdue University Libraries, Karnes Archives and Special Collections, Purdue Buildings and Campus Scenes
source_evidence.measurement_method: Visual reference only. Photograph shows a prominent vertically framed entry block with light-colored vertical elements, adjoining long horizontal wings with repetitive glazing, and masonry walls.
source_evidence.uncertainty: The image is historic and undated. It does not reveal present-day additions, façade orientation, measured bay spacing, or the present entrance location. The model's uniform window bay pattern and north-facing portal placement are schematic.

source_evidence.measurement_method: The department lists Lilly Hall of Life Sciences, 915 Mitch Daniels Blvd.
source_evidence.uncertainty: Address corroborates identity only; it does not verify a particular entrance door.

geometry_and_validation.source_coordinate_transform: EPSG:3857 -> geographic lon/lat -> project local frame X east / Y north, origin 40.4274, -86.9137; approximate conversion per modular/AGENTS.md

remaining_uncertainty: The service's numeric floor and roof fields have no published unit metadata; 25.05 m overall height is estimated from R=82.2 interpreted as feet.
Only a historical archival exterior photograph was found. Current elevation drawings, verified entrance coordinates, and contemporary roof articulation were not available.
The GIS footprint provides a single continuous outline. The model preserves it exactly but does not infer unseen courtyard voids or variable roof heights.
